title: [Mode] UV EDITOR
content: ### Objective To edit UV for mapping 2D textures on patterns. ### Location Window ▶ UV Editor (Ver. 2025.0) Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ UV Editor (ver. 2025.0) UV Editor mode button on the toolbar at the top of the window. (up to Ver. 10) ### Operation Access the UV Editor from the Location above. Back and Side UV can be exported as UV. (Ver. 2025.0) #### [Definition of UV screen, coordination, and tiles] ![UV_Editor.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437954503577) Horizontal axis: U Vertical axis: V A square of one U/ V: Tile UV snapshot saves each Tile as a single image. The coordinates of the tile are determined by the coordinates of U and V and are the same as the UV coordinates inside each tile on the image above. #### [Definition of Wire] ![UV_Editor_wire.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438003616537) Wire is the mesh line (Polygon) of UV. Wire image will be saved when saving UV. **Show UV Wire (Ver. 7.5)** **Location:** UV Editor Mode Popup menu (Right-click on background) Show Wire The existing textures are hidden and UV Wire (meshes) are displayed. **Rendering View Settings (ver. 9)** The toolbar contains rendering options. Diffuse, Metalness, Normal, Roughness Map. **View UV Maps (ver. 10)** 1. Upper left of the UV Editor window ▶ Click the View UV Map icon → Map icons that can be changed appear horizontally. 2. Click the desired map icon. → The UV of the 2D window changes to the type of map users click. ※Note: The UV map of the OBJ topstitch used in a garment is also provided. (ver. 11) View and Bake Displacement Map is now available (ver. 11) **Texture Repeat Type (ver. 10)/ Texture Mapping (ver. 11)** If the Texture Repeat Type of the fabric is set to Unified Map, changing the position of the UV in the UV Editor Window moves the textures in 2D and 3D patterns to the textures in the changed location. Fabric Properties | Description ---|--- Texture Repeat Type (ver. 10)/ Texture Mapping (ver. 11) | Unified Map (ver. 10) / Unified (ver. 11) | Display the texture based on the pattern layout of the UV map. [Repeat UV Settings] * Repeat U: Size the texture based on U direction. * Repeat V: Size the texture based on V direction. The number 1 means that the texture is repeated once between 0-1 of the UV map. **Move UV with Value (ver. 11)** 1. UV Editor Toolbar ▶ Click the Move UV tool. → Move UV window appears. 2. Set the distance to be moved. Distance 1 indicates the length of the segment of the UV Tile in the UV Editor window. 3. Move the UV by clicking the Arrow icon or pressing the directional keys on the keyboard. → UV is moved according to the distance you set.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for accessing and utilizing the UV Editor in version 2025.0 for editing and mapping 2D textures on patterns.

title: [MODE] UV EDITOR: Bake Textures
content: ### Objective Bake selected texture. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ UV Editor Mode ▶ Tool Bar ▶ Bake Textures Tool ### Operation 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location above. → The Bake Textures setting window will be displayed. 2. Set values according to the table below. **Bake Textures Detail Setting Table** Saving Path | Click folder button to set the file path and save path. Select PNG either JPEG file format. With PNG save option, the background will be transparent. With JPEG save option, the background will be black. ---|--- Size (pixels) | Set the size of the image to be saved. Images are stored in squares of the same horizontal and vertical size. Fill Texture Seams (ver. 2024.1) | Set how many pixels to pad the UV shells by. Min: 1 ~ Max: 256 Pixels Infinite Seams (ver. 2024.1) | UV Seam Padding is extended to infinity. UV area | 0-1 (Default) | Save default 0 to 1 tile. A tile is a rectangular area for one section of one unit. Selected tile | Save a specific tile. Input U, V location to be saved. All tile | Save all tiles that contain UV. Fill Texture Seams | The outline is filled with texture as you enter the pixels. Texture type | Select texture types to be saved. 3\. After setting the details, click the "Save" button at the bottom. → The image is baked and saved to the path you set. ※ Note: * When baking, the seamline normal map will be baked together. (ver.10) * The UV map of the OBJ topstitch used in a garment is also provided. (ver.11) * UV padding pixel value can be adjusted using Fill Texture Seams value. The extended seam can also be set to infinite and will not invades other UV shells. (ver. 2024.1) ![UV_Seam_Padding.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438158205081) **View UV Maps (ver. 10)** 1. Upper left of the UV Editor window ▶ Click the View UV Map icon → Map icons that can be changed appear horizontally. 2. Click the desired map icon. → The UV of the 2D window changes to the type of map users click. ※ NOTE: View and Bake Displacement Map is now available (ver. 11)
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for using the Bake Textures tool in the UV Editor to effectively create and save texture maps for 3D models.

title: Topstitch Style Property Editor (ver. 2025.0)
content: Topstitch Style Property Editor Topstitch Property Editor Topstitch Context Menu * * * ## Topstitch Style Property Editor ### Objective Use these options to edit Topstitch styles and materials. **** ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ (Select) Topstitch Style ▶ Property editor ### Operation Object Browser ▶ Select a topstitch item in the Topstitch Tab. → The properties are displayed in the Property Editor. Properties | Description ---|--- Information | Name | Enter a name for the Topstitch. | Type | Select either OBJ to create a 3D mesh, or Texture to apply the effect as a material. Offset | Select the Offset distance from the dropdown menu in inches, or enter a value in millimeters in the input box. Stitch Count | Select between 1 and 5 stitches. For multiple stitches, you can apply unique material properties to each one. Enable Use Same Specification to apply identical settings, or Use Same Material to use the same material settings across all stitches. Specification | Shape | Select the type of topstitch from the drop-down icon. Click the plus + icon to[ register the topstitch as an OBJ file **(link here)**.](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358155220249) Click the CONNECT icon to open the CONNECT Store and download buttons. OBJ | Texture Bartack | ![bartack_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438335426713) | ![bartack.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438330503577) Buttonhole | ![buttonhole_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438335994649) | ![buttonhole.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438336244761) Single | ![topstitch_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438331382169) | ![default.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438331645081) Overlock | ![overlock_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438337029145) | ![overlock.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438337328281) Pickstitch | ![pickstitch_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438337596185) | ![pickstitch.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438332674969) Zigzag | ![zigzag_render.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438338110873) | ![zigzag.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438417186585) Set the Length (SPI), Space, and Thread Thickness of the Topstitch. ※Note: SPI stands for Stitch Per Inch, meaning the number of stitches within an inch. For example, 'SPI-4' means there are four individual stitches within an inch. For standard garments, SPI-11 is often used. Material Button / Thread | Type | Set the appropriate fabric type for the topstitch. ---|---|--- Base Color | Color | Select the color of the base color. Base Color Map | Base Color Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from the Library/Folder. Desaturate | Desaturate the entire Base Color Map to remove color and convert it into grayscale or black and white. Switch | Color Switch: Easily and quickly switch the color of the texture to a new one without losing the accuracy of the chosen color. ![Switch Color.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438338582553) ※Note: For consistent results, the Base Color Map should contain 1 color. If the Base Color Map contains multiple colors, users may experience unexpected results. Normal Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from the Library/Folder. Generate with the PBR texture generator icon. Intensity | Adjust the intensity of the Normal map from -100 to 100. Displacement Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from Library/Folder, generated with the PBR texture generator icon. Amount | Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. The white area of the displacement map shows the maximum height. Shift | Adjust the distance between the displacement map and the garment surface Clipping | Adjust to delete all geometries below the Clipping value. Particle Distance | Adjust the Particle Distance of newly created meshes. Keep Continuity | Extend the adjacent face to eliminate the boundary line. ※ Note: Only applicable to Welded OBJs. Opacity | Adjust the opacity level from 0 to 100. Opacity Map | RGB Mode | The encoded map with alpha value in the RGB channel. Alpha Mode | The encoded map with the alpha value in the alpha channel. Reflection | Roughness | Intensity | Edit fabric gloss by adjusting the Intensity of the Roughness Map | Edit fabric gloss by adding and modifying the Roughness Map. Map | Select the Browse button next to the Map option to add a Roughness Map to the selected Fabric style. Map Intensity | Adjust the Map's Intensity. Invert | Select to invert the gloss of the fabric. When this option is selected, the shiny part becomes dull and vice versa. Reflection Intensity | The greater/lesser the Reflection Intensity value is, the more reflective/dull the material or fabric is, and vice versa. Metalness | Adjust the metallic level. A higher value makes the surface more metallic. Metalness Map | Partially express metallics using a grayscale image. The white parts of the map appear metallic. Configuration | Face | Select the Face of Topstitch. Number of Lines | Set how many lines of Topstitches there are for a single style. Distance | It is possible to adjust the distance between the lines. The unit of length can be set in inches, millimeters (mm), or centimeters (cm). 3D | The Topstitch is more realistic in the 3D window. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438417580057) ## Topstitch Property Editor ### Objective Use these options to edit topstitch styles: * Extend: When the start or end point of a Topstitch does not reach or stick out of the Pattern outline, extend it to fit to the outline of the Pattern. * Corner: Set the Topstitch corner type to extend the stitch more smoothly at corners. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Topstitch ### Operation Find the menu from the location above, and select a topstitch line in the 2D pattern window. → Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. Property | Description ---|--- Name | Rename Topstitch. Topstitch Property | Select the Topstitch to edit its properties. Extend | Turn On/Off the settings in Start / End. Corner | Curved | When turned On, the selected Topstitch is now curved and smoothly extended. ![rightangledcorner.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438417837593) ※ Note: Corner settings only apply when connecting with Free Topstitch Sewing. Right Angled | When turned On, the selected Topstitch is now a right angle. Z Offset (mm) | Enter a value in millimeters to set the offset from the pattern surface. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438417580057) ## Topstitch Context Menu ### Objective Use these options to manage topstitch, including deleting and renaming. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Topstitch ### Operation Right-click a button in the location panel to rearrange the topstitch list. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- Delete | Deletes the selected Topstitch style. ※Note: You can also delete them with the Delete Topstitch on the keyboard. A Topstitch Style can only be deleted if there is no Topstitch assigned to it. Delete All Unused Topstitches | Removes unused Topstitches from the Topstitch list. Rename | Rename the Topstitch style. Reset | Resets the properties of the Topstitch style to the Default Topstitch properties.
content_description: The Topstitch Style Property Editor page provides comprehensive tools for editing and managing topstitch styles and materials in your design projects.

title: GoZ for Marvelous Designer
content: GoZ Install Run GoZ from Marvelous Designer Run GoZ from ZBrush * * * ## ## Objective GoZ allows direct Import and Export of objects between Marvelous Designer and ZBrush. ## GoZ Install Download the installer using the links bellow. * [**Latest GoZ installer for Windows**](https://s3.amazonaws.com/s3.md.web.upload/marvelousdesigner/GoZ_for_Marvelous_Designer_Windows_1.0.0.zip) * [**Latest GoZ installer for MacOS**](https://s3.amazonaws.com/s3.md.web.upload/marvelousdesigner/GoZ_for_Marvlous_Designer_macOS_1.0.0.zip) ※ Note: * The above GoZ installer works with Marvelous Designer (ver. 2024.2 and above) and is compatible with ZBrush 2022 and later. * To access archived version of GoZ for Marvelous Designer 2024.1 and below (for Windows), please download the installer from the link below: * [**[Archived] GoZ installer (Windows)**](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47657221196313) **Install GoZ for Marvelous Designer from ZBrush** 1. Unzip the downloaded zip folder (md_goz_app_[OperatingSystem]_[VersionNumber]), then install GoZ to ZBrush by moving the contents in \MarvelousDesigner\ folder to the following directory: * * Window default directory path: C:\Users\Public\Pixologic\GoZApps\MarvelousDesigner\ * MacOS default directory path: /Users/Shared/Pixologic/GoZApps/MarvelousDesigner/ * ※ Note: For MacOS, after moving the contents in \MarvelousDesigner\ folder to the directory above, go into MarvelousDesigner folder. Please unzip GoZBrushToMarvelousDesigner and GoZInitMarvelousDesigner. 2. After you unzip the "MarvelousDesigner" folder to GoZApps folder, run ZBrush. 3. Go to ZBrush Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ GoZ ▶ path to MarvelousDesigner. 4. In the list displayed, click the version of Marvelous Designer you will be using. 5. If a Security Warning pop-up window appears ▶ click Run. 6. Click 'Install' Button to start GoZ Marvelous Designer installation. ※ Note: * Please Click Replace if file already exist in the GoZApps\MarvelousDesigner folder. * If you have multiple versions of Marvelous Designer installed, please note that the newly revamped GoZ for Marvelous Designer is only available for Marvelous Designer version 2024 and above. * You can verify that the path to the Marvelous Designer executable file is correct by checking in the GoZ_Config.txt file located in the GoZApps\MarvelousDesigner folder. **Reinstall GoZ for Marvelous Designer from ZBrush** 1. Preform Force Reinstall by going to ZBrush Main menu ▶ Preferences ▶ GoZ ▶ Force Reinstall 2. In the list of GoZ enabled application, select Marvelous Designer. 3. Click 'Install' Button to start GoZ Marvelous Designer installation 4. If a Security Warning pop-up window appears, click Run. ※ Note: To ensure GoZ plugin is working properly with Marvelous Designer, please keep the default name for Marvelous Designer application as it is, and do not modify its name. * * * ## Run GoZ from Marvelous Designer After installing GoZ for Marvelous Designer, you can directly export Garments, Avatars, Trims and Scene and Props from Marvelous Designer with the Run GoZ menu. #### **Location** Main Menu ▶ GoZ ▶ Export to ZBrush #### **Operation** 1. Make sure Path to Marvelous Designer is correctly setup with the version of Marvelous Designer in use in ZBrush. 2. Select elements in the scene (Avatar/Garment/Trim/SceneAndProps) to be exported to ZBrush. 3. Go to Main Menu ▶ GoZ and select Export to ZBrush. 4. In the pop-up window, in Object tabs, you can add and remove scene elements to export. 5. Set export setting and click OK button. 6. Go to ZBrush, drag in the 3D window. 7. In Subtool, you can find Patterns + Trim become a single tool, scene and prop become a single tool, and each avatar becomes a tool of its own. 8. PolyGroups are automatically assigned: * * Pattern: split per pattern shapes. * Avatar: split per component. * Trim: split per Trim object. * Scene and Prop: split per Scene and Prop. #### Export to ZBrush Settings Object | Select All Patterns * Select/Deselect all Patterns. * Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Avatars * Select/Deselect all Avatars/Objects. * Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Trims * Select/Deselect all Trims. * Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. Select All Scene and Props * Select/Deselect all Scene and Props. * Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. ---|--- #### Unweld Exports Vertex(points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects. | #### Weld Combines Vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts together as one point. #### Thin Ensures thickness is not exported to Geometry even if the value is increased beforehand. | #### Thick Exports thickness value to Geometry. Basic | Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported with a unit of measurements. Scale % | Works on top of the unit of measurement above, scale by specific percentage value. * Reset: Reset all settings to Default. ※ Note: * For Avatar and Scene and Prop, selecting a part of an object will have the corresponding object in the object list to be selected. * Selecting only the body of an avatar will result in the entire avatar being selected in the Export to ZBrush dialog. * * * ## Run GoZ from ZBrush You can directly export object to Marvelous Designer from ZBrush through GoZ. #### **Location** Tool ▶ ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438736204697) #### **Operation** 1. Set Import Settings in Marvelous Designer from Main Menu ▶ GoZ ▶ Import Settings 2. Under Tool window, make sure Marvelous Designer is set as the current GoZ enabled application by clicking the "R" button shown in the image above.![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438736364825) 3. Click GoZ button to export currentSubTool to 'GoZ' enabled application, or use the shortcut Ctrl+G 4. Click All button to export all SubTools to 'GoZ' enabled application, or use the shortcut Ctrl+Shift+G 5. Click Visible button to export visible SubTools to 'GoZ' enabled application. 6. Once the object is exported by GoZ, you can see mesh are imported to Marvelous Designer based on Import Setting #### GoZ Import Settings Basic | Load Type | Open | All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported file only. ---|---|---|--- Add | Add files and keep the existing objects. Object Type | Avatar | Import file as an Avatar type. \- Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim | Import file as Trim type. \- For more information on Trim Type, check out [Trim Properties](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187139609) Page Garment | Import an Object as Simulation ready Garment, physical properties can be adjusted from the property editor. Scene and Props | Import file as Scene & Props. \- For more information on Scene & Props, check out [Scene and Props Properties](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358290160921) Page Scale | Adjusts scale of file being exported with a unit of measurements. Scale % | Works on top of the unit of measurement above, scale by specific percentage value. Axis Conversion | It is possible to specify which of the X, Y, or Z axes should be designated as the Up axis. Translation | Align Bottom to Ground | Position the bottom of the imported object on the ground plane. * Reset: Reset all GoZ settings to Default. ※ Note: * After importing mesh as garment using GoZ, some features in Property Editor (such as Mesh Style and thickness rendering, etc.) remain editable but not effective since the imported item is treated as a mesh rather than a pattern.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide detailed installation and operational guidelines for the GoZ plugin, facilitating seamless import and export of objects between Marvelous Designer and ZBrush.

title: Connect Store (ver.11-2024.2)
content: ### ### ### Objective Now you can either purchase or download garment items from the Store within the Marvelous Designer Software. (Windows/MAC) ### Location Select the Store Tab on the left side of the screen. ※ Note: As of Ver 2025.0, it has been integrated into the New Library Window. * [_**New Library (Beta)**_](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358127622809-New-Library-Window-2025) ▶ CONNECT Assets (ver. 2025.0) ### Operation The Store is only available when signing-in with your account registered on www.marvelousdesigner.com Left click the Sign In icon on the top right hand corner of the screen to login. ### Menu | ### Description ---|--- ### Item List : All items in the store appear. | * Hover your mouse over an item to see its name and price * You can click like icon on any item you like or add it to the cart. * Key-in what you want in the search bar at the left top of the screen * You can search by entering keywords in the search bar. * Use the Filter to view items in a desired category. * Items can be sorted in a desired order, using the 'Sort By' drop-down menu at the upper right-hand corner. * Turn 'Don't show owned item' on in order not to view what you have already purchased. (Available for those who sign-in.) ### Detail : See the details of any selected item. | * Double clicking an item to view the detailed information. * The seller name can be found below the name of an item. * You can select the license type to purchase, either 'Basic' or 'Extended', and find the description of the license at the bottom. * Click the '3D Viewer' button to view the item in 3D. * After selecting a license for the item, click the 'Add to Cart' button to add the item to your cart. * You can find the tags and descriptions of the item. (Only available when registered by the seller.) * Item images edited by the seller are also available. * Click the arrow icon on either side of the image, or select the page number at the bottom, to navigate through additional images.. ### Cart : Check the items added in the Cart and buy them. | * You can check the total quantity and price of your items, and delete any items you don't want to purchase. * Click the 'Checkout' to bring up the purchase page. ### My Item : Check the items purchased and download them. | * All items you have purchased appears as a list. * Click the 'Download' to download any purchased item.
content_description: Discover and access a wide range of garment items for purchase or download directly from the Marvelous Designer Store, easily navigable through the integrated New Library Window.

title: Auto Convert to Motion (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ### ### Objective Convert FBX files from external platforms into motion files for Marvelous Designer Avatars. Converted motions are compatible with all Marvelous Designer Avatars. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Auto Convert to Motion ### Operation 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. → Auto Convert to Motion window appears. → Mode is Switched to Animation Mode immediately to check the converted motion. ※Note: An error occurs when Avatars already exist in the 3D window. 2. Select the Gender of the avatar to be converted, open the Motion File (FBX) and click Convert button. You can open FBX files downloaded from platforms such as Mixamo, or your own custom animation file. → Convert it to motion for Marvelous Designer Avatars. 3. Click Play in the Animation Editor to check the converted motion. 4. Click the Save button to save as motion file (MTN). ※ Note: To Move the Avatar and Garment to the location of the first frame of converted motion, load the saved motion file.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a step-by-step guide for converting FBX files into compatible motion files for Marvelous Designer Avatars, ensuring seamless integration of animations into your designs.

title: Puckering (ver 2024.0)
content: Create puckering Apply Puckering Edit Puckering Puckering Style Properties Assign Puckering Style Puckering Style Properties Show/Hide Puckering ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Create puckering You can create puckering on pattern outlines, inner line segments, and sewing lines. ### ## Apply Puckering ### Objective Apply puckering textures, including normal and base color maps for detailed surface definition and fold points at seams to create realistic-looking fabric gathers and wrinkles along seamlines. ### Operation **Segment Puckering** Select a line segment to create puckering. 1\. Select the Segment Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu → Materials → Puckering → Segment Puckering 2D Window Toolbar → Segment Puckering 2\. Click the segment you want to create a puckering for. **Free puckering** You can create puckering on pattern outlines and internal lines regardless of segment points. 1\. Select the Free Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu → Materials → Puckering → Free Puckering 2D Window Toolbar → Free Puckering 2\. Set the first and last points on the line where you want to create the puckering by clicking the mouse. **Seamline Puckering** You can create a puckering on a pattern seamline. 1\. Select the Seamline Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu → Materials → Puckering → Seamline Puckering 2D Window Toolbar → Seamline Puckering 2\. Click on the Sewing Line to create the puckering. ### End Result → Puckering is created on that line. → You can see the puckering created on the 3D Garment. → For Seamline Puckering, the puckering will appear on one or both Sewing Lines depending on the 'Placement' set in the Puckering Properties. ※Note: In the 2D window, you can create puckering in one step by clicking and dragging an area to include all the desired line segments. Puckering cannot be created twice. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Edit Puckering You can select and modify the puckering applied (move the position, modify the length/width). ### Operation 1\. Select the Edit Puckering tool via the path below. Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Puckering ▶ Edit Puckering 2D Window Toolbar ▶ Edit Puckering Object Browser ▶ Select the Puckering Icon in the Object Browser (Ver. 2025.0) ![Screenshot 2025-04-15 132418.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438147484697) 2\. Click & drag to select the line segment or Left-Click on the puckering line to edit the puckering. 3\. To delete the puckering, select the puckering line and press the Delete key on the keyboard. ### End Result → Move Position: Select & drag the puckering line to move the entire line. → Modify Length: Click and drag the end point of the puckering to modify the length. If you right-click while editing the length, a Moving Distance dialogue will appear, allowing you to move it to the desired numerical value. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Puckering Style Properties Set the properties of a Puckering Style. ### Operation 1\. Select a puckering object / line with the Edit Puckering tool. The Properties are displayed in the Property Editor beneath the Object Browser. Edit the selected puckering. **Puckering object properties** **Property** | **Description** ---|--- Name | Changes the name of the puckering object. Puckering Property (ver. 2025.0) | Changes the puckering style. Extend | Extends the start/end of the puckering to the outline of the 2D pattern. Offset | Offset | Adjusts the distance the puckering is spaced from the pattern outline. Include or exclude the width of the puckering from the spacing as needed. Z Offset | Adjust the Z-axis distance of the puckering. Placement | Both Sides | *For Puckering on Internal Lines only. Check the box to have Puckering appear on both sides of the Internal Line. Flip | *For Puckering on Internal Lines only. Check the box to flip the puckering to the other side of the internal line. 2\. Another option is to right-click on the applied puckering with Edit Puckering active to apply the options as needed. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- Select All With the Same Property | Selects puckering with the same styles as the selected puckering. Assign to New Puckering | Adds and applies a new puckering style. Delete | Deletes the puckering. ※Note: You can also delete by pressing the Delete key on your keyboard. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Assign Puckering Style Applies the Puckering style to the selected Puckering lines. ### **Apply with a generated Puckering style** 1\. When generating Puckering: After selecting a Puckering style in the Puckering window, it will be applied as the selected style when generated. 2\. Apply after Puckering is created: Select a Puckering line and click the 'Apply' button to the right of the Puckering style. **Apply as a new Puckering Style** 1\. Select a Puckering line and add it with the 'Assign' button at the top of the Puckering window. 2\. Select a Puckering line and add it to the 'Assign to New Puckering' menu from the right-click menu. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438164865433) ## Puckering Style Properties You can adjust the properties of the Puckering style to achieve different forms of puckering. When you select a Puckering Style in the Puckering window, the Puckering Style properties appear in the Properties window. title: Quick Pinching /Advanced Pinching with Soft Selection (Ver. 2025.0)
content: ## Quick Pinching ### Objective Like the existing pinching feature, Quick Pinching allows for fast and simple pinching by pulling the mouse-picked point as a single point. ### Location Quick Pinching is automatically activated while simulation is running: * Quick Pinching (Q): It is executed by default when the simulation starts. * 3D Tool Bar ▶ Drop-Down Menu ▶ Quick Pinching (Ver. 2025.0) ![Selectmove.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438152064025) ![SelectQuickPinch.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438152167833) ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438199330713) ## Advanced Pinching ### Objective Advanced Pinching is an evolved version of Quick Pinching that allows for precise pinching based on the user's desired area and fall-off settings. ### Location Advanced Pinching can be activated while simulation is running: * **Ver. 2025.0:** 3D Tool Bar ▶ Pinching Drop-Down Menu ▶ Advanced Pinching ![SelectAdvancedpinching2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438152548121) * **Up to Ver. 2024.2:** 3D Background Context Menu (Right-click 3D background) ▶ Advanced Pinching (Shift + E) ### Operation (2025.0) 1. Load a garment into the scene. 2. Activate Simulation and select the Select/Move Tool ( Q ). 3. (With simulation active) Select Advanced Pinching from the Location above. 4. The Advanced Pinch Settings dialog window will pop up _(see images below)_ 5. In the Option section, adjust the following tool options to your preference: ### Operation (up to ver. 2024.2) 1. Load a garment into the scene. 2. Activate Simulation and select the Select/Move Tool ( Q ). 3. (With simulation active) Right-click the background in the 3D Window to bring up the 3D Background Context Menu. 4. Run the Advanced Pinch (Shift + E) option. 5. The Advanced Pinch Settings dialog window will pop up _(see images below)_ 6. In the Option section, adjust the following tool options to your preference: Range | The shape graph reflects the selected Falloff(Shape * Distance * Power) and cannot be manipulated directly. ---|--- Falloff Shape | Select the Falloff Shape: Bump or Linear ![falloff shape.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438138557465) Falloff Distance | Set the distance of the selection range to the radius: Min/max: 1-500(mm) ![Visual indicator of falloff distance.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438138699289) Falloff Power | A value that sets the strength of falloff. Min:-2.0 Max:+2.0 ![4869aa7f-745f-4861-a5c8-64257497e6bf.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438153202201) Options | Distance Measure | How the distance from the picking point is measured. Surface | When multiple layers of patterns are together, only one independent layer will be selected. Straight | Select all patterns within a certain distance from the picking point regardless of the layer selected. Distance Indicator | Indicates the Falloff Distance/Power values using 2 concentric circles around the pinch icon. When turned off the circles will disappear. ![78de1a69-72a1-4cc6-acc5-2031751e5df2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438216650393) Limit to Selected Patterns | When selected only one pattern will be affected regardless of whether the Distance Measure is Surface or Straight. ![999a90e8-8b62-4bab-ae88-7a84bb454b03.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438167297049) Display Weights | Displays a contrasting color to the mesh where the weight value is applied. ![2d28e3ff-3eea-412a-a077-ee328038e99b.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438201394073) Modify the Range and Option values and freely pinch the patterns.

title: Add Pattern Thickness
content: ### ### Objective Extrude garment to express thickness. Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express doubled sided effect. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 4. Property Editor ▶ Geometry → Modifies the Geometry Properties which will affect mesh style / extrusion direction when exporting with thickness. #### Geometry Properties Add'l Thickness - Rendering (mm) | Displays the added thickness in addition to the Thickness value of Fabric Style. ---|--- Extrusion Direction | Sets the direction to display the thickness. Both | Apply the thickness front/rear around the pattern. Forward | Apply the thickness in the front direction of the pattern. Backward | Apply the thickness in the rear direction of the pattern. Toggle each side on or off to determine whether to generate the Mesh. (ver. 2025.0) Front Face | Set whether or not the front part is displayed based on the normal direction. Back Face | Set whether or not the back part is displayed based on the normal direction. Seam Face | Set whether or not to show overlapping sides on the sewn line. Side Geometry | Curvature (%) | Set side geometry lateral curvature percentage. Resolution | Set divisions for the side mesh. Double Side | Apply Curvature attribute values to both front and back symmetrical from the pattern. UV Expansion (ver. 2025.0) | The Side and Back UVs can be edited in UV Editor. [**Video here**](https://youtu.be/6e8yRsHUv_8) Back Face | Check this on to show the back face UV. Side Face | Check this on to show the side thickness UV. Mesh Style | Triangle | Re-mesh the pattern using triangular mesh option Quad (Optimized) | Re-mesh the pattern using quadrangular mesh option. Generates aligned automatic Retopology results. Quad (Grid) | Re-mesh the pattern using quadrangular mesh option. Generates pattern with a uniform grid. Face Count | Display total face count of the pattern. Vertex Count | Display total vertex count of the pattern. ※ Note: To use UV Expansion, Thick Textured surface must be active in the 3D window. ### Operation (Ver. 2024.1 and below) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern / Transform Pattern 2. Select a Pattern or Pattern line to express doubled sided effect. → Its properties appear in the Property Editor. 3. Property Editor ▶ Selected Line ▶ Curved Side Geometry ▶ Check on Double Sided → The selected Pattern or Pattern line is now being displayed as double sided.

title: Quadrangular / Triangular Mesh
content: ### Objective Convert synchronized 3D Garments into quadrangular or triangular mesh structures. ※Note: Please refer to the below explanation on different usages of Quadrangular Mesh versus Triangular Mesh. As the program speed may differ due to their intrinsic characteristics, please select the most appropriate Mesh Type based on your needs. To use our program most efficiently, however, we strongly suggest you set all Pattern Mesh to Triangular when editing 3D Garments. Then, change ONLY the necessary Patterns' Mesh type to Quadrangular to complete the Garment. * When to Use Triangular Mesh: All Cases, except for exceptional cases, needed to use Quadrangular Mesh. * When to Use Quadrangular Mesh: When a detail of a 3D Garment needs to round smoothly, such as a shirt collar or piping. ### Location Right click on a pattern (3D window) → Triangulate/Quadrangulate Right click on a pattern (3D window) → Mesh Style → Triangle/ Quad (Optimized) (ver. 2024.0) Pattern Property Editor → Geometry → Mesh Style → Triangle/ Quad (Optimized) / Quad (Grid) (ver. 2025.0) Pattern Property Editor → Miscellaneous → Mesh Typ → Quad / Triangle Pattern Property Editor → Mesh → Mesh Style → Triangle/ Quad (Optimized) (ver. 2024.0) Pattern Property Editor → Geometry → Mesh Type → Triangle/ Quad (Optimized) / Quad (Grid) (ver. 2025.0) ※Note: Improved the algorithm for the Rectangle (Optimize) feature. title: Why do I have to pay tax?
content: **Question** I am VAT registered. Why do I have to pay tax? **Answer** Please note that if you have a correct registered VAT ID, you can add VAT ID on Billing Address and your tax will be waived Since January 2019, CLO Virtual Fashion LLC(Marvelous Designer US office) has officially been registered VAT MOSS(Sales Tax) in Ireland(EU). \- Since our online license sales are handled by our US office, all of our Individual license pricing will be in effect, according to the regulation below. From January 2015, new legislation came into force that affects the sale of digital services to customers in other EU countries. Digital services include broadcasting, telecommunications, and electronic services(which includes software products). The VAT rate that is calculated for this type of transaction is based on a place of supply the service. The legislation that is regulating MOSS rules is: * [Council Directive (EU) 2017/2455](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32017L2455&from=EN) \- supplies of services and distance sales of goods (VAT e-commerce package). * [Council Directive 2008/8/EC](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:L:2008:044:0011:0022:EN:PDF) \- a place of supply of services. * [Council Implementing Regulation (EU) No 1042/2013](http://eur-lex.europa.eu/LexUriServ/LexUriServ.do?uri=OJ:L:2013:284:0001:0009:EN:PDF) \- place of supply of services. This means if your billing address is under the EU region, VAT rates for each country will be added to your purchase. title: Trims
content: ### Objective Modify existing Trims and apply them to garments with the following features. * Glue Trim * Tack on Trim * Delete Trim * Transform Trims * Set Trim Stiffness * Right-Click Options Menu * Trim Simulation Recording ※Note: * To learn how to import OBJ as Trim, please refer to articles [3D File (OBJ) Import/Export](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358223288601), [3D File (FBX) Import/Export](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232885017) and [Trim Style Window (Ver. 2024.1)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358161655705) * To Learn and modify Trim Properties, please refer to the [Trim Properties](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187139609) page. * With the current versions, Trim Simulation with Collision only works with CPU Simulation. This does not work with GPU simulation at this time. * * * ## ## Glue Trim ### Objective Glue 3D Trims onto Garments and simulate together (ver 3.0.0). ### Operation #### Glue Trim 1. Click the loaded Trim with the Select/Move tool. → Gizmo for the selected OBJ appears. 2. Click on the Glue icon next to the OBJ Gizmo, then mouse over the desired location. → preview tags along the mouse. 3. Click on the desired location. → Selected trim automatically attaches to the place. 4. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and angle. ※ Note: To cancel the arrangement, press Esc on the keyboard. 5. Activate Simulation. → Trim is now being simulated along with the rest of the Garments. ※Note: You can select multiple trims and move or rotate those by using Gizmo. (ver. 11 ) * * * ## Tack on Trim (ver. 2025.0) ### Objective Attach trims to desired locations on by using the tack tool to apply them to multiple points across and various patterns. ### Operation 1. Using **Select/Move** tool in the 3D toolbar, click ![Direct Positiong.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438151583513)**Direct Positioning** next to the Gizmo. 2. Hover over the pattern and click the desired location. 3. Using **Tack** tool in the 3D toolbar, Click on an initial point on the trim. 4. Click on the desired point on the garment. * Repeat the step to tack the trim to multiple points 5. Click the Simulate tool. ※Note: Tack is not available on deactivated trims. * * * ## Delete Trim ### Objective Delete selected Trims ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D viewport 2. Click Delete key on Keyboard to remove. → Selected OBJ is now being removed from the Garments. 3. Delete trim can also be done through the right click options menu. * * * ## Transform Trims ### Objective Transform trim as needed. ### Operation #### Via the Scale Gizmo Click and drag on the X, Y, or Z-axis to transform the Trim. Axis | Description ---|--- X-Axis | The red axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the x-axis to transform the trim along its x-axis. Y-Axis | The yellow-green axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the y-axis to transform the trim along its y-axis. Z-Axis | The blue axis of the Gizmo. Click and drag the z-axis to transform the along its z-axis. Square | The yellow square located in the center of the Scale Gizmo. Click and drag the square to transform the trim, while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. → The trim is transformed. When the trim transformation is complete, click the Scale button again. → The Gizmo used for moving and rotating trims appears. #### Via the Property Editor through [Trim Style Window](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358161655705) 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Trim 2. Select the trim style to be transformed. → The properties of the trim appear in the Property Editor. 3. Find the Scale option. 4. Enter the desired value for the below options. Option | Description ---|--- X-Axis | Enter the desired x-axis value. Y-Axis | Enter the desired y-axis value. Z-Axis | Enter the desired z-axis value. Maintain Ratio | Toggle this option on to adjust an OBJ while maintaining its x, y, and z ratio. * * * ## Set Trim Stiffness (ver. 2024.2) ### Objective Semi-Elastic Trim can be achieved when reducing stiffness value. ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D window. 2. In the Property Editor, adjust Stiffness Value. → When Stiffness Value is reduced, the trim will be slightly bent when sufficient force is applied. → To get more rigid Trim simulation, increase the Stiffness Value. ※Note: The Stiffness of the trim can only be set when the trim material is in the "active" state. * * * ## Right-Click Menu ### Objective Set extra Trim Options include Trim Simulation toggles, Unglue, refresh Trim Textures and export selected Trim to USD layer. ### Operation 1. Select Trim in the 3D viewport. 2. Right-click on the selected Trim. → Trim is now being selected and Trim Options pop-up menu appears. #### Trim Options Select All Trims | Select all Trims in the 3D window. ---|--- Delete | Delete selected Trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Del Copy | Copy selected trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + C Paste | Pasted copied trim. \- or use keyboard shortcut: Ctrl + V Simulation (ver. 2024.2) | Freeze | Freeze selected trims. \- Trim collides with garments but maintain the 3D position with no gravity influence. Activate | Activate simulation on selected trims. \- Trim collides with garments and influenced by weight and gravity. Deactivate | Deactivate selected trims. \- Trim does not collide with garments and maintains it’s 3D position. Unglue | Unglue trim from garment if glue function is applied. \- This option will not be available if glue function is not applied. Hide Trim | Hide selected trim or trims. Refresh Textures | Refresh selected trims textures. Export to USD Layer (ver. 12.1) | Export Trim to USD authoring layer, or create a new USD file with the selected trims. \- To learn more on USD export and USD layer editor in Marvelous Designer. Please move to [USD file Compatibility](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358343098777) page. ※Note: * To copy and paste multiple trims, hold down the Shift key on the keyboard and select all trims to be copied, then perform the procedure above. * When copying and pasting multiple trims, they must all be placed within a Pattern. * * * ### Trim Simulation Recording (Ver. 2025.0) When recording garment animation, the simulation cache of the Trim is recorded a separate layer from the Pattern, under the descendant of the Garment Layer.

title: Marvelous Designer File Format
content: ### Marvelous Designer File Format Type | Format | Description ---|---|--- Garment | [*.zpac](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358279381529) | Contains information on Garments, Patterns, Sewing, and Fabrics. Project | [*.zprj](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358219651225) | Compresses the various files used for Garment creation into one file, and saves it. The Project file contains the AVT file that has Avatar-related data [Avatar, Accessories, Arrangement Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points, Avatar size, Poses] and the ZPac file that contains Garment-related data [3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Fabrics, subsidiary Material], as well as an animation file if there is animation. Avatar | [*.avt](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358359735961) | Contains all the information related to Avatars (Model, Sizing data, Poses, Motions, Accessories, Bounding Volumes, Arrangement Points). Avatar (Encrypted) | [*.avte](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187017113) | Encrypted MD/CLO avatar file types. This file type cannot be exported,[ This includes the Metahuman Body Types found in the Avatar folders. ](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358187017113) Pose | [*.pos](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358350508697) | Avatar Pose information that, automatically saved whenever the Garment is saved. The Avatar’s Pose can easily be changed with this file. Avatar Poses from other software can only be saved when the Avatar is a COLLADA file with joints. Joint Motion | [*.mtn](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358363172249) | Contains Avatar Motion information. As with the Pose file, can only be saved on COLLADA file Avatars with joint and Animation information. Fabric | [*.zfab](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358267968153) | Contains the property values (texture + physical properties) of the set Fabric. Physical Property | [*.psp](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358434392857) | Contains the detailed values of Fabric Physical Properties. Topstitch | [*.sst](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358389918873) | Contains the type, number of lines, thread thickness, SPI, length, etc. Button | [*.btn](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358452715161) | Contains the type, size, and color of Buttons. Buttonhole | [*.bth](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358452715161) | Contains the tyle, size, and color of the Buttonholes. Arrangement Point | [*.arr](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358280634905) | Arrangement Points are the blue points that are distributed around the Avatar, and are used to arrange Patterns easily around the Avatar. Arrangement Points are created on top of the Arrangement Bounding Volume covering the surroundings of the Avatar. Arrangement Bounding Volume | [*.pan](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358365447705) | Arrangement Bounding Volumes are the green cylinders covering each part of the Avatar, and each end of a cylinder is connected to an Avatar’s joint. As such, even if the Avatar’s Pose is changed, the cylinder simply adjusts to the changed Pose and can be used as it is. Tape Measure | *.mea | It has the information of the tape measure created in the avatar. Camera Projection | *.cmp | Contains the camera's Field of View information (near, far, etc.). Camera Transformation | *.cmt | Contains camera view information of the 3D Garment window. Simulation Property | [*.smp](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358232630937) | Contains settings for Simulation.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive overview of the various file formats used in Marvelous Designer, detailing their specific functions and contents related to garment creation and avatar management.

content: ### Objective Apply 2D image files to express the surface texture of fabric. ### Operation #### Via Drag and Drop 1. Open a folder that contains the desired texture image in your file browser. 2. Drag and drop the texture image onto a pattern in the 2D or 3D window. → The texture of all patterns using the same Fabric will have the new texture applied. ※ Note: * If a texture image is already applied, the existing texture image will be replaced when applying a new texture image via drag and drop. * Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to the Open icon next to the Texture menu in the Property Editor (Ver. 4.0.0). * Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to an object in the program, then select the correct map: texture, normal, specular (Ver. 4.0.0). * After Base Color Texture image is applied, maps for Displacement, Opacity, Roughness, and Metalness channel can be automatically generated using PBR Map Generator (ver. 2024.1). * If using a Base Color Map with an alpha (to transmit transparency) and Opacity Map are applied at the same time, the alphas of both are reflected in the transparency result (ver.2024.1) * Before (Ver. 2024.1) when the Base Color Map and Opacity Map were applied at the same time: only the alpha of the Opacity Map was reflected in the transparency expression, not the alpha of the Basecolor Map. Now the alpha of both maps is applied (Ver. 2024.1) * You can now "open your Texture File with Another App" (this is found under Property editor ▶ material ▶ Base color ▶ base color map ▶ ellipsis (**...**) for quick editing (Ver. 2025.0) #### Via Property Editor * Select a Fabric to apply a texture image to from the Fabric tab in the Object Browser. * Follow the path: Property Editor ▶ Fabric ▶ Texture Open button. → The Open File window appears. * Find and select the desired texture image from the file browser, then load. → The selected texture image is now applied to the Fabric.
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on how to apply 2D texture images to fabric surfaces using drag and drop or the Property Editor in our design software.

title: Avatar Properties
content: ### Objective Set the Avatar's properties, such as skin style, eye direction, skin friction, and color of body elements. ### Location 3D Window ▶ Select Avatar ▶ Property Editor ### ### Operation Set the Avatar's properties. When you select an avatar, its properties appear in the property window. **Avatar Properties** **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name** | Enter a name and an item number for the avatar. **Size** | Lists the size Preset chosen from the Avatar Editor. **Body Styling** | **Skin Style** (Ver. 2025.0) | Set the appearance of the avatar from presets or Customize You can manually set the color of hair, skin, underwear, eyebrows, eyes, and lips by clicking the Style Configurator button on the right. **Eye Control** (Ver. 2025.0) | **Horizontal** | Adjust the position of the avatar's eyes horizontally. **Vertical** | Adjust the position of the avatar's eyes vertically. **Surface** | **Skin Offset** | Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of meshes, a very high particle distance and a low Skin Offset value can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. ※ Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, as the simulation will slow down when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. **Static Friction** | The friction setting when a garment is in a stationary position. **Kinetic Friction** | The friction setting when a garment is moving. **Soft Body Simulation** (Ver. 2024.0 and above) | Apply a deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity When recording animations, Defualt Adult Avatar animations with soft body simulation are recorded separately and can be exported to Alembic Cache. For other formats, they will only be exported based on the current frame. ※ Note: * When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. * Avatar-type objects that are not rigged can also be simulated. (2025.1) * NVIDIA GPU is supported starting from version 2025.2. **Soft Body Stiffness** | Min - Max: 5,000 - 10,000 The smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. **Divide Mesh** (Ver. 2025.0) | Subdivides the mesh of the avatars to smooth the surface of the avatar. Values are between 1 and 3. Use this feature only when necessary. The denser you set the mesh, the slower the simulation will run. E.g., This works best when you drape a fitted garment, such as leggings, since a low-density avatar mesh may be visible. **Material (Selected)** | Set the [Material](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425) of the selected part of the avatar. For Example: select the eyes and adjust color, base color map, etc. **Miscellaneous** | **Mesh Type** | Indicates the type of selected avatar mesh. **Element Count** | Indicates the number of points in the selected mesh. **Avatar Properties (ver. 2024.2)** **Properties** | **Description** ---|--- **Information** | **Name** | Enter a name and an item number of the avatar. **Model** | You can change the type of avatar. **Surface** | **Skin Offset** | Adjust the distance between the avatar and the garment. Since the avatar and the garment consist of the meshes, a very high value of particle distance and low value of Skin Offset can cause the avatar to protrude out from under the garment. To prevent this, the default Skin Offset value is set to 3mm, which is the proper value for creating a garment. When you fit your garment accurately or create a fitted garment, lower the value of the Skin Offset. ※ Note: Leave the default value until you almost finish your garment, since the simulation is being slow when you lower the Skin Offset of the avatar and the Particle Distance of the garment. **Static Friction** | The friction when a garment is in stationary position. **Kinetic Friction** | The friction when a garment is moving. **Soft Body Simulation** (ver. 2024.0) | Apply deformable body simulation to express skin elasticity When recording animations, avatar animations with soft body simulation are recorded separately and can be exported to Alembic Cache. For other formats, they will only be exported based on the current frame. ※ Note: When Soft Body Simulation is on, a button is displayed in the bottom right corner of the 3D window to indicate its activation status. **Soft Body Stiffness** | Min - Max: 5,000 - 10,000 The smaller the value, the smoother the simulation. **Material**(Selected) | Set the [Material](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358364198425) of the avatar. **Miscellaneous** | **Mesh Type** | Indicates the type of avatar mesh. **Element Count** | Indicates the number of points in the mesh. **Smooth Avatar** | **Smooth** | Toggles the Smooth option on or off. If the option is on, the mesh on the avatar's surface will be divided as set in 'Division Level'. **Division Level** | Can be split by a factor of 1 to 5. **Soft Body Simulation (ver. 2024.0)** **Soft Body for Custom Avatars (ver. 2025.1)**

title: Lock
content: ### Objective Use respective lock functions to easily select and edit Patterns or Internal Lines/Shapes. For example, lock all Patterns to easily select Internal Lines/Shapes and vice-versa. ### Location #### Lock All Patterns Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Lock ▶ Lock All Patterns Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Lock All Patterns #### Lock Selected Patterns Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Lock Pattern #### Lock All Internal Lines Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Lock ▶ Lock All Internal Lines Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Lock All Internal Lines ### Operation #### Lock All Patterns 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Lock ▶ Lock All Patterns Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Lock All Patterns →All Patterns are deactivated as they turn translucent. 2. Click and drag or select the desired Internal Lines/Shapes. →Only Internal Lines/Shapes and no Patterns are selected. 3. To unlock Patterns, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Lock ▶ Unlock All Patterns Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Unlock All Patterns #### Lock Selected Patterns (ver5.0.0) 1. Select Transform Pattern or Edit Pattern tool. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Lock Pattern → The selected Pattern outlines and Internal lines are locked and cannot be selected. → Locked Pattern outlines and Internal lines turn grey. 3. To unlock Patterns, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Lock ▶ Unlock All Patterns Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D Window) ▶ Unlock All Patterns #### Lock All Internal Lines 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Lock ▶ Lock All Internal Lines Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Lock All Internal Lines →All Internal Lines are deactivated as they turn translucent. 2. Click and drag or select the desired Patterns. →Only Patterns and no Internal Lines/Shapes are selected. 3. To unlock Internal Lines/Shapes, follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Lock ▶ Unlock All Internal Lines Right Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Unlock All Internal Lines

title: Register Topstitch (2025.0)
content: OBJ Topstitch Texture Topstitch ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438090016537) ## Register OBJ Topstitch ### **Objective** Save custom OBJ files as a Topstitch in a *.sst format file type. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Style Window ▶ Default Topstitch Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Style Window ▶ Default Topstitch Viewport Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Style Window ▶ Default Topstitch ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Default Topstitch → Properties of the selected Topstitch appear in the Property Editor. 2. Please check that your OBJ meets the requirements below before attempting to register an OBJ as a Topstitch. * Position the face of an OBJ towards the Y-axis. * Position the contact point of an OBJ where it should be attached to 3D garments at 0,0,0 (x,y,z) coordinates. * The unit of OBJs must be in mm. 3. Select the button on the right of OBJ to load your custom Topstitch ![Screenshot 2025-04-24 152353.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438104147097) 4. Select the button on the right of OBJ to load your custom Topstitch. ![Screenshot 2025-04-24 152425.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121155225) 5. Press OK ※Recommended: Please maintain the number of vertices of an OBJ below 1000 to avoid speed issues. The distance between an OBJ and the ground should be 0. (You can adjust the distance in Marvelous Designer) ## ![Screenshot 2025-04-24 152425.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438121155225)![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438090016537) ## Register Texture Topstitch ### **Objective** Save customized Topstitch object or texture files in a *.sst format file. ### **Location** Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Default Topstitch ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Topstitch Tab ▶ Default Topstitch → Properties of the selected Topstitch appear in the Property Editor. 2. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Type and select Texture from the drop-down menu. 3. Under the Material section, select the same structured Topstitch as the one customized. 4. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture and click the Topstitch image icon or the Search button. → The Open file window appears. 5. Find the path to the customized images and select the one only with the name of Topstitch (ex. "zigzag.png") and click Open. → The program automatically saves all five images in a *.sst file according to the defined naming rule. → The image is loaded in actual size, which is approximately 2cm. It may look bigger than other preset Topstitches. 6. Navigate to the Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Preset and enter the desired value in the Stitch Width menu (ex. 5mm) to adjust its size. 7. On the top right of the Property Editor, there is a Save button. Select to save. → The Save file window appears. 8. Enter the desired name and location and save. → The Topstitch is now saved in the *.sst file format. ※ Note: Topstitches are classified into two different types depending on the presence or absence of the Stitch Width property. For example, when adding zigzag-style top stitches, select Overlock or Zigzag as its width needs to be adjustable. Without Width Property | Default (Single Needle) ---|--- Default Offset 0 Pick Stitch With Width Property | Overlock Zigzag Buttonhole Bar Tack * Ensure all of the Topstitch image files are located in the same path, as it will not be saved in the SST file properly. * The image is bigger than the actual size to prevent distortion in resolution when enlarging the image. * Drag and drop the saved SST file directly onto the Topstitch Item List or open it by pressing the Open button in the Property Editor. Adjust the property details such as the Length, Offset, Thread Thickness, or Color. ##
content_description: This webpage provides detailed instructions for registering custom OBJ files and textures as Topstitch in the *.sst format within the Marvelous Designer software.
